governance.note: 2026-08-02: ArcAdminTimelock's admin (the role that can change who may propose/execute, or transfer admin again) was migrated from the deployer EOA to a freshly-deployed 2-of-3 ArcMultisig (contracts/src/ArcGovernance.sol) via transferAdmin/acceptAdmin — verified on-chain, admin() now returns the multisig. isProposer/isExecutor were left as the deployer alone (routine timelock operations stay single-key; only the higher-privilege admin role required 2 signatures to change). ArcMultisig itself has NO owner-rotation function — its signer set is immutable once deployed, so this is a one-shot decision. All 3 signer keys were generated on and are stored on the same VPS that runs this project (not independent devices/parties) — this multisig protects against a single lost/misused key, not against compromise of this server itself. See docs/ARCODIAN-AUDIT-READINESS.md; ArcAdminTimelock's own contract docstring still says 'Not audited, not for mainnet' — this migration does not change that.
